{{Short description|American anthropologist}}
{{For|the neuroscientist and psychiatrist|Jeffrey M. Schwartz}}

'''Jeffrey Hugh Schwartz''' (born March 6, 1948) is an American [[Physical anthropology|physical anthropologist]]<ref name="thinkers">{{cite news|url=http://www.post-gazette.com/stories/local/uncategorized/the-thinkers-pitt-anthropologist-thinks-darwins-theory-needs-to-evolve-on-some-points-435990/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024213156/http://www.post-gazette.com/stories/local/uncategorized/the-thinkers-pitt-anthropologist-thinks-darwins-theory-needs-to-evolve-on-some-points-435990/|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 24, 2012|title=The Thinkers: Pitt anthropologist thinks Darwin's theory needs to evolve on some points|date=May 29, 2006|work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|last=Belko|first=Mark|accessdate=November 3, 2017}}</ref> and [[professor]] emeritus of biological [[anthropology]] and History and Philosophy of Science at the [[University of Pittsburgh]] in [[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania|Pittsburgh]], [[Pennsylvania]], and a fellow and President of the [[World Academy of Art and Science]] (WAAS) from 2008 to 2012.

Schwartz' research involves the methods, theories, and philosophies in [[evolutionary biology]], including the origin and diversification of [[primates]].  He has studied and analyzed human, primate, and fossil skeletal material focusing much of his research on dental and skeletal morphology.  He has done fieldwork and museum research in the collections of various major museums around the globe.

==Work, research, and recognitions==
In the revised and updated publication of ''[[The Red Ape: Orangutans and Human Origins]]'', Schwartz argues there is additional evidence for his contention that [[orangutan]]s share significantly more morphological similarities to humans than does any other great ape.<ref name="orangutan">{{cite news|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/news/science/2009/06/18/pitt-prof-orangutans-not-chimps-our-closest-relative/stories/200906180460|title=Pitt prof: Orangutans, not chimps, our closest relative|date=March 15, 2012|work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|access-date=November 3, 2017}}</ref>

He has also been a major contributor to the [[George Washington]] project, an attempt to create wax figure likenesses of the first U.S. president at the ages of 19, 45, and 57, based upon craniofacial morphology.<ref name="George">{{cite news|url=http://www.post-gazette.com/stories/news/science/3-d-recreations-by-pitt-anthropologist-bring-new-dimension-to-first-president-597703/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160412182205/http://www.post-gazette.com/science/2005/08/28/3-D-recreations-by-Pitt-anthropologist-bring-new-dimension-to-first-president/stories/200508280214|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 12, 2016|title=3-D recreations by Pitt anthropologist bring new dimension to first president|date=August 28, 2005|work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|last=Spice|first=Byron|accessdate=November 3, 2017}}</ref> On public display in a new education center and museum at [[Mount Vernon (plantation)|Mount Vernon]], the models also went on a 9-city national tour to promote the museum.<ref name="GeorgeTour">{{cite news|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/lifestyle/2010/02/14/Meet-the-first-president-at-History-Center-exhibit/stories/201002140299|title=Meet the first president at History Center exhibit|last=Barcousky|first=Len|date=February 14, 2010|work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|access-date=November 3, 2017}}</ref>

Since 1998 he has served as a consultant in forensic anthropology to the [[Allegheny County, Pennsylvania|Allegheny County]] coroner's office and later the Medical Examiner Office of the same county.<ref name=thinkers/>

In 2007 he was elected President of the [[World Academy of Art and Science]] for a five-year term (one year as president-elect).  He was the first person so elected, all previous presidents having been directly appointed by trustees of the organization.<ref name="Pittnews">{{cite news|url=http://www.news.pitt.edu/news/pitts-anthropology-professor-jeffrey-schwartz-elected-president-world-academy-art-and-science|title=Pitt's Anthropology Professor Jeffrey Schwartz Elected President of World Academy of Art and Science|date=February 27, 2007|accessdate=November 3, 2017}}</ref>

==Education==
Born March 6, 1948, in [[Richmond, Virginia]], Schwartz earned his bachelor's degree from Columbia College in 1969 and completed his doctorate from [[Columbia University]] in 1974.<ref name=thinkers/>

==Family==
Schwartz is the son of Jack Schwartz, a physician who conducted [[quinine]] research during World War II,  and [[Lillian Schwartz]], one of the earliest visual artists to utilize computer imaging.<ref name="inaugural">{{cite news|url=http://www.worldacademy.org/?q=Installation_Remark_by_Prof_Jeffrey_H_Schwartz|title=Installation Remark by Prof. Jeffrey H. Schwartz|work=World Academy of Art & Science|publisher=[[archive.is]]|date=February 28, 2008|accessdate=November 3, 2017|url-status=bot: unknown|archiveurl=https://archive.today/20130616045522/http://www.worldacademy.org/?q=Installation_Remark_by_Prof_Jeffrey_H_Schwartz|archivedate=June 16, 2013}}</ref> He is married to the [[poet]] [[Lynn Emanuel]] and they reside in Pittsburgh.

==Film==
Jeffrey H. Schwartz made an appearance in the documentary film ''[[The Trouble with Atheism]]''. He was also featured on the Daily Show with John Stewart opposite Evolutionary Biologist and noted TV personality Todd Disotell.
